title: Understanding Selection Bias
text: Selection bias occurs when the sample is not representative of the population. Consider how the method of selecting every fifth student might lead to a biased sample.

title: Impact of Sampling Method
text: Think about whether the students attending the discussion sections are representative of all UC Berkeley students. Could this method exclude certain groups?

hintAnswer: The sample may not represent all students, as it only includes those attending discussions.
title: Identifying Potential Bias
text: What could be a potential issue with selecting students based on their attendance in discussion sections?
choices: The sample may not represent all students, as it only includes those attending discussions.
There is no issue with selecting students this way.
This is an example of selection bias.

hintAnswer: No, it may not be representative as it depends on the order of students attending.
title: Evaluating Representativeness
text: Does selecting every fifth student ensure a random and representative sample of the entire student body?
choices: No, it may not be representative as it depends on the order of students attending.
Yes, since all students are selected randomly.
